---
title: "How suggestions work"
description: "Shared mechanics of the bot suggestion workflows."
---

Three workflows propose changes to your package instead of just checking
it: [DESCRIPTION authors](authors-suggest.qmd),
[roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and
[test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd). They share how
their changes reach you. What happens inside the roxygen and test
workflows, step by step, is shown [under the hood](suggestions-internals.qmd).

## Suggestions are pull requests, never direct commits

A bot never commits to your branch. When a workflow has something to
suggest for your PR, it

1. commits each changed file separately on a branch
   `bot-suggest/<kind>/<your branch>`;
2. opens a pull request from there **into your feature branch**;
3. comments on your PR, e.g.

   > **Roxygen documentation suggestions** opened: #19 (into `feat/my-feature`)
   >
   > 2 changes applied · 1 not applied
   >
   > - `R/ds.wrapper.R`

   The other titles are "Test suggestions" and "Update contributors in
   DESCRIPTION".

You review the suggestion like any PR: merge it, edit it first, or close
it. New pushes to your PR update the same suggestion PR instead of opening
another one.

## Sweeps {#sweeps}

The roxygen and test workflows also have a `scan-mode: all`, meant for a
monthly schedule: they review the **whole package** on `dev` (the
`sweep-base` input) and collect everything in one pull request into `dev`
from `bot-suggest/<kind>-sweep-YYYY-MM`. Running a sweep again in the same
month updates that month's pull request. The test workflow limits each
sweep to recently changed functions plus a rotating share of the rest, see
[sweep scope](test-suggest.qmd#sweep-scope).

The example callers switch mode by trigger, so one file handles both:

```yaml
    with:
      scan-mode: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'changed' || 'all' }}
```

GitHub stops scheduled workflows in repositories without activity for 60
days — add the [workflow keepalive](workflow-keepalive.qmd) so the sweeps
keep running.

## What gets proposed {#what-gets-proposed}

A suggestion should be a real improvement, not a reworded sentence or an
extra test for its own sake. So Claude has to state a **reason** for every
change, from a fixed list, and only some reasons lead to a proposal:

| Workflow | Proposed | Dropped |
|---|---|---|
| Roxygen | `missing`, `inaccurate`, `incomplete` | `clarity`, `style` |
| Tests | `uncovered_branch`, `error_handling`, `edge_case`, `regression` | `other` |

On top of that, the workflows drop documentation changes that differ only
in whitespace, punctuation or case, and tests whose assertions already
exist. The lists are set as `accept_reasons` in `config/claude.yml` and can
be [changed per repository](#adjusting-the-guidance). They are a first
setting, likely to be tuned.

The test workflow also changes **existing tests**, but only for fixed
reasons: an update when the function's behaviour was changed on purpose
(`contract_changed`), a deletion for a duplicate, removed behaviour or a
trivial test. A test that fails because the code may be wrong is only
reported. See [existing tests](test-suggest.qmd#existing-tests).

## Housekeeping

- The bot never reviews its own pull requests: the suggestion workflows skip
  any PR from a `bot-suggest/*` branch.
- [Cleanup suggestion branch](cleanup-suggestion-branch.qmd) deletes a
  `bot-suggest/*` branch once its pull request is merged or closed.
- With the [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app) configured, your
  required checks run on suggestion PRs; without it they don't, and a
  ruleset requiring them would block the merge.

## Adjusting the guidance

The workflows read their settings, guidance and prompts from this
repository. To change one for your package only, put a file at the **same
path** in your repository — it is used instead of the shared one:

| File | Controls |
|---|---|
| `config/bot-authors.json` | Accounts never added to `DESCRIPTION` |
| `config/claude.yml` | Claude model, request settings and `accept_reasons` |
| `config/report-style.yml` | Heading levels and spacing of the suggestion reports |
| `config/roxygen-style.json` | Roxygen tag order and per-tag guidance |
| `config/test-role-guidance.json` | Testing strategy given to Claude |
| `config/workflow-outcomes.yml` | What workflows produce, for the [workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd) |
| `prompts/*.md` | The full prompts sent to Claude |

Start from a copy of the shared file, since yours replaces it completely.
